query: How will we define sampling frames and operational procedures for household versus street‑connected populations, eligibility screening, migrants/transients, and nonresponse/replacement?

response.query: How will we define sampling frames and operational procedures for household versus street‑connected populations, eligibility screening, migrants/transients, and nonresponse/replacement?
response.answer: Sampling frames for household populations use census data; for street-connected, use outreach programs. Operational procedures include eligibility screening via surveys and verification. Migrants/transients require mobile units; nonresponse/replacement uses follow-up calls.

results.title: Employer Payment for Personal Protective Equipment
results.content: The Final Rule Codifies an Employer Payment Requirement Implicit in the OSH Act and the Wording of the Existing PPE Standards Many Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) health, safety, maritime, and construction standards require employers to provide their employees with protective equipment, including personal protective equipment (PPE), when such equipment is necessary to protect employees from job-related injuries, illnesses, and fatalities. In this rulemaking, OSHA is requiring employers to pay for the PPE provided, with exceptions for specific items. In 1999, OSHA issued a proposal to require employers to pay for all protective equipment, including personal protective equipment (PPE), with explicit exceptions for certain safety shoes, prescription safety eyewear, and logging boots (64 FR 15402). 5.  OSHA does not require employers to keep records of employees' requests to use their own PPE. 6.  Some employees in agriculture are covered by two general industry standards, the logging standard (29 CFR 1910.226) and the cadmium standare (29 CFR 1910.1027), which specifically require employers to pay for required PPE.
